title: Momentum Transfer Lab: Camera-Mat Collision Table
description: A physics sandbox where an antique camera and a coffee mat sit on a frictionless table surface. The user configures mass, velocity, and elasticity parameters for each object, then launches collision experiments to observe conservation of momentum and kinetic energy. An undo/redo system lets the user step back through experiment configurations while a real-time dashboard tracks momentum and energy totals.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader from CDN. Load AntiqueCamera.glb and coffeemat.glb, scaling them to roughly similar visual sizes (camera ~0.4 units, mat ~0.5 units). Place both on a flat rectangular table (a box geometry with wood-like MeshStandardMaterial). Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0,4,6) looking at the origin, with OrbitControls for viewing. Add ambient light (0.4 intensity) and two directional lights from opposite sides. Implement a custom physics engine (no external library): each object has configurable mass (0.5-5 kg via slider), initial velocity vector (X and Z components, range -5 to 5 m/s via sliders), and a global elasticity coefficient (0-1 slider, 0=perfectly inelastic, 1=perfectly elastic). The interaction flow requires 10+ steps: (1) select the camera object, (2) set its mass, (3) set its X-velocity, (4) set its Z-velocity, (5) select the coffee mat, (6) set its mass, (7) set its X-velocity, (8) set its Z-velocity, (9) adjust elasticity, (10) press Launch to simulate. After launch, animate both objects moving and colliding using sphere-based bounding collision detection. On collision, compute post-collision velocities using conservation of momentum and the elasticity coefficient. Display a real-time HUD panel showing: total momentum vector (should be conserved), total kinetic energy (conserved only when elasticity=1), and per-object velocity vectors. Add Undo and Redo buttons that store each parameter change in a history stack, allowing the user to step backward and forward through configurations. Add a Reset button to return objects to starting positions. Include a Launch Count display. Objects should bounce off table edges with reflection. Use requestAnimationFrame for smooth 60fps animation. Style the control panel as a semi-transparent overlay on the left side with clearly labeled sliders and buttons.
